japanese_black.windows: the device_lp_point plan: same blocks, 100 ms ticks, point-sampled labels, purity and windows as --preprocess device_lp_point (the plan does not depend on the filter)
japanese_black.features: M0's transform on those windows: mean of the raw, unfiltered samples within +-50 ms of each tick (100 ms bins centred on the ticks); no other filter
japanese_black.purpose: matched-window comparison: same windows and labels as device_lp_point, only the preprocessing differs

filter.design: scipy.signal.butter at fs = 25 Hz (bilinear, pre-warped: -3 dB at the cutoff)
filter.initial_state: steady state at the first sample of each block
filter.approximation: The exact MPU6886 DLPF response is not known. This filter only matches its documented 3 dB bandwidth (5.1 Hz for A_DLPF_CFG=6 [to verify] against the datasheet). Order 1 is chosen because the documented noise bandwidth / 3 dB ratio (7.8 / 5.1 = 1.53) is close to a first-order filter (pi/2 = 1.57), not a 2nd-order Butterworth (1.11). The chip filters a ~1 kHz signal; content above the dataset's Nyquist frequency cannot be reproduced. Raw samples are treated as evenly spaced.

point_sampling.rule: nearest raw sample to each 100 ms tick (value and native label); no averaging
point_sampling.missed_tick: ends the block (the firmware drops a window with a sample > 20 ms late)
